=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- docs/plans/review-blocked-approval-gate-trust-scope-plan.md:70-77 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: D3 never defines trusted automation bot identities, so pipeline-authored PRs and comments with user.type == "Bot" fail the trust test.
  WHY: Implementing D3 literally forces approval for the pipeline-authored PR population, contradicting the stated goal and tests; all four reviewers agree on the defect.

- docs/plans/review-blocked-approval-gate-trust-scope-plan.md:75-77; 367-369 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: The case-sensitive REVIEW_BLOCKED_APPROVAL_PROTECTED_PATHS default lists only agents.md and does not protect consumer repos' AGENTS.md.
  WHY: A trusted-author PR changing only AGENTS.md would not match the protected-path list and could merge without approval; all four reviewers agree on the gap.

- docs/plans/review-blocked-approval-gate-trust-scope-plan.md:323-329 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: Phase 2 step 10 targets recovery_action_for_phase and _candidate_details_json, but managed-wave recovery uses detect_stalls and recover_stalled_issue instead.
  WHY: Implementing the step as written skips only the standalone path, so current-wave issues labeled ai:awaiting-human-approval can still retrigger review and dispatch the judge; the reviewers agree on the managed-path omission.

- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:6784-6791 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The approval_pending case arm does not set JUDGE_ACTION to approval_pending before emitting the message.
  WHY: The workflow can continue to the generic *) fallback and re-emit the CRITICAL alert instead of suppressing it.

- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:6784-6791 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The approval_pending case does not export MSG for the subsequent tg_send_tracked call.
  WHY: Telegram notification delivery can use an empty or stale message.

- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:6784-6791 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The approval_pending case does not ensure JUDGE_ACTION and JUDGE_SKIP_REASON are correctly set on every path entering the case statement.
  WHY: Unset or unexpected values can cause duplicate alerts or misreported state.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: PR description and plan Goals bullet at lines 163-167 say "a same-repo PR authored and commented on only by trusted principals … executes … with no human comment", and the Tests bullet at lines 417-419 say "the next review-blocked PR authored by the pipeline merges without a comment".
  expected_change_site: `docs/plans/review-blocked-approval-gate-trust-scope-plan.md` D3 Chosen block (lines 70-77) and Phase 3 step 15 helper spec (`scripts/gh_helpers.sh` `review_blocked_approval_required`)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: No diff hunk in D3 names a trusted bot identity allow-list; Phase 3 step 15 enumerates reasons `mode_always, action_close_and_reissue, fork_head, untrusted_author, untrusted_commenter:<login>, protected_path:<path>` but no `trusted_bot_login:<login>` reason and no allow-list seed; the plan's Goals and Tests bullets assume the helper treats `user.type == "Bot"` with a trusted login as "trusted", but the helper spec does not encode that test.

- requirement: Plan §18.E / §14 requires the change to reach consumers on the next `@stable` tag via the workflow-templates wrappers; "Files & Modules" lists the workflow files but Phase 3 step 18 (lines 367-369) introduces `REVIEW_BLOCKED_APPROVAL_MODE` and `REVIEW_BLOCKED_APPROVAL_PROTECTED_PATHS` as new repo variables that the consumer wrappers `workflow-templates/ai-review.yml` and `workflow-templates/ai-orchestrate-poll.yml` would need to forward.
  expected_change_site: `docs/plans/review-blocked-approval-gate-trust-scope-plan.md` Phase 3 step 18 (lines 367-369) and Files & Modules block (lines 385-408).
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: No explicit step enumerates the wrapper-template edits required for consumer propagation; the deferred "if they forward vars explicitly" clause silently allows consumers on `trust-scoped` to silently revert to `always` if their wrapper doesn't forward the new vars. The plan also does not document the behaviour the wrapper must implement when the var is unset on a consumer (i.e. fallback to `trust-scoped` vs. fail-closed to `always`).

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- docs/plans/review-blocked-approval-gate-trust-scope-plan.md
  Line or code reference: D3 Chosen, lines 70-77 (rule block) and Goals bullet, lines 163-167 (and Tests bullet, lines 417-419)
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: D3 declares the trust test as "the PR author is not a GitHub `User` with `author_association` in `OWNER`, `MEMBER`, `COLLABORATOR`; any PR issue comment or review comment author fails the same test". GitHub's `user.type` for a pipeline-authored PR is `"Bot"` (e.g. `codex` / `codex-bot` / `github-actions[bot]`), so `user.type != "User"` is true for every pipeline PR.
  WHY: a Phase 3 implementation that takes D3 verbatim evaluates every `Bot`-typed author and commenter as "untrusted" and emits `untrusted_author` / `untrusted_commenter:<login>` reasons, so trust-scoped mode silently degenerates to "always" mode for the dominant PR population.

- docs/plans/review-blocked-approval-gate-trust-scope-plan.md
  Line or code reference: D3 Chosen default list, line 75-77; Phase 3 step 18 default string, lines 367-369
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `REVIEW_BLOCKED_APPROVAL_PROTECTED_PATHS` default lists only `agents.md` (lowercase).
  WHY: The planned path match is case-sensitive, so a same-repo trusted-author PR whose only diff is a consumer-cased `AGENTS.md` slips past the protected-path rule.

- docs/plans/review-blocked-approval-gate-trust-scope-plan.md
  Line or code reference: Phase 2 step 10, lines 323-329 (stall skip) versus Phase 2 "Files & Modules" lines 385-408
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Phase 2 step 10 says the stall skip should be inserted "before `recovery_action_for_phase` is applied in the managed and standalone stall loops", but `recovery_action_for_phase` is only ever called from the standalone ladder.
  WHY: The managed-wave path uses `recover_stalled_issue()` and `_dispatch_rb_judge_for_pr`, so a current-wave managed issue carrying `ai:awaiting-human-approval` still emits `retrigger_review` and fires the judge.

=== FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 6784-6791
  severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `approval_pending` case arm does not set `JUDGE_ACTION` to `approval_pending` before emitting the message, so the generic `*)` fallback would still fire if the workflow continued past this block.
  WHY: The workflow would fall through to the default `*)` case, re-emitting the same CRITICAL alert instead of suppressing it.

- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 6784-6791
  severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `approval_pending` case does not export `MSG` for the subsequent `tg_send_tracked` call, so the message variable remains empty or retains a prior value.
  WHY: The Telegram notification would send an empty or stale message instead of the intended alert text.

- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 6784-6791
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `approval_pending` case exits with `exit 0` on reuse, but the workflow does not ensure that `JUDGE_ACTION` and `JUDGE_SKIP_REASON` are set correctly for all code paths leading into the case statement.
  WHY: If those variables are unset or carry unexpected values, the case arm may not behave as intended, potentially leaking duplicate alerts or misreporting state.
=== END FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
